text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alert: elevated 5xx rate from model-serving runtime (segfault/oom signals) across eu-west-1. Triggered by >500 errors in last 3m. Pager routed to #incidents and current on-call.

iris_oncall: seeing ~18% 5xx on gateway for /v1/generate, spike started ~00:02 UTC. Grafana shows runtime crash loops on model-runner pods.

julia_sre: confirming, some pods in CrashLoopBackOff with `SIGSEGV` in logs. Repro on two different host GPU types (A100, T4). Collecting logs.

mike_infra: pulling logs now. `kubectl -n inference logs model-runner-@pod -c runner --previous` shows repeated stack:
```
[runner] 2026-03-15T00:03:10Z segfault at 0x7f8c1a2b
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```
Also kernel OOM messages on node: `oom_killer invoked` for `model-runner`.

sam_prodeng: Is this tied to recent quant-kernel change we rolled out last night? deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-14T22:10 (quant-opt v2) to canary and prod.

deploy-bot: Rollout record: `canary=30% -> success`, `prod=100%` at 22:10. No automatic rollback triggered.

katie_support: Customer-impact channel: several enterprise customers report timeouts and retries, some request failures. I'll flag high-touch customers.

iris_oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback quant-opt v2, 2) route traffic to fallback model-variant (fp16), 3) scale up warm fallback pool. Proposing (2) + (3) first for minimal blast radius.

julia_sre: agreed. Initiating traffic reroute: will update routing policy to prefer model-variant `redwood/model-base-fp16:2026-03-10` and reduce batch_max_tokens for new requests.

mike_infra: applying patch to routing layer now:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/{model}
{ "fallback": "model-base-fp16", "prefers": ["model-base-fp16"], "batch_max_tokens": 512 }
```

iris_oncall: executed. Confirming traffic shift... gateway metrics show slow decrease in 5xx but some pods still crash on older sessions.

sam_prodeng: running a controlled rollback of quant-opt v2 on model-runner clusters in eu-west-1. Starting at 00:10 UTC.

deploy-bot: Rollback job started (ID: rb-20260315-001). Rolling nodes sequentially.

mike_infra: while rollback proceeds, I'm disabling aggressive KV-prefetch which might be exacerbating memory growth. Patch applied to runtime config on affected nodes.

julia_sre: core dumps collected: uploading to /mnt/incident-dumps/3765432100/. Adding symbolicated stack traces to the incident doc.

iris_oncall: customer-impact update: ~12% of requests for customers on eu-west-1 experienced 5xx between 00:02 and 00:09. No data exfiltration. Support will notify top 5 customers with ETA.

customer-impact: draft message posted to top customers: "We experienced elevated errors in EU region due to runtime crashes following a runtime optimization. We have mitigations active and are rolling back the change. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause." :white_flag:

ops_lead: good. Keep me updated. If rollback doesn't stop crashes within 10m, escalate to full prod rollback and open SEV.

julia_sre: after rollback of quant-opt v2 to v1.7 on 8/10 nodes, crash rate reduced. Last crash events correlate with approx 30s window prior to rollback completing.

mike_infra: confirmed memory usage per runner dropped ~40% after rollback + disabling KV-prefetch. No further OOM kills in last 6m on patched nodes.

iris_oncall: gateway 5xx rate down to 1.3% from 18% peak. Latency slightly increased on fallback model but within SLO for most customers.

sam_prodeng: plan next: create hotfix branch to guard against kernel path in quant-opt that touches huge allocations for long sequences. Add runtime cap and fail-safe to fallback earlier.

julia_sre: opening follow-up ticket: RUNTIME-5123 "quant-kernel large-allocation path -> OOM/SEGV on heavy long-seq workloads". Attach core dumps and traced inputs as repro.

katie_support: outreach in progress to affected customers. No escalations to legal/infosec.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=high, impact=partial (eu-west-1), start_ts=3765432100, mitigation=traffic-reroute+rollback, status=mitigated->monitoring.

iris_oncall: handing off to julia for post-incident analysis and on-call for next 2 hours. @julia_sre you own the postmortem and RCA.

julia_sre: taking handoff. Will run extended soak tests on A100 + T4 with long prompt sequences and enable additional memory checks. ETA initial RCA summary 6h.

mike_infra: scheduling a canary rollout with memory-safety checks and incremental grad(3) rollout to ensure this doesn't reoccur. Also adding OOM early-detection alert to oncall playbook.

iris_oncall: thanks all. closing live mitigation loop. Keeping thread open for RCA updates and customer followups. :white_check_mark:

katie_support: marking customers notified. Will attach any responses to the follow-up ticket.

julia_sre: initial RCA notes (will expand in full postmortem): quant-opt v2 introduced a prefetch path that allocates large pinned buffers for long sequences; under certain sequence length distributions we hit fragmentation + unexpected allocation failure leading to std::bad_alloc + subsequent segfault in optimized kernel. Fix is to bound prefetch allocations and add graceful fallback to CPU or fp16 kernel.
